ConocoPhillips fell 0.8% today, extending a sharp decline from earlier in the week when the stock dropped from $140.52 to $134.40 in just two days. The primary driver appears to be the collapse of climate negotiations at the UN's COP31 summit on Sunday, where governments rejected a draft deal that failed to address fossil fuels—a symbolic setback for oil majors seeking regulatory clarity, even though the immediate business impact is unclear. Adding pressure, analysts noted that the "epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding" as of today, signaling a shift in market appetite away from energy plays that had recently outperformed.

The stock is also caught between conflicting forces: crude oil prices remain reasonably firm (US oil at $89.53/barrel), but geopolitical tension in the Middle East—with Houthis attacking Saudi refineries and Iran-backed strikes continuing—has not provided the typical upside that supply disruptions might otherwise deliver. This suggests the market is repricing energy stocks on sentiment and rotation rather than on crude fundamentals alone.
